label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.104…… supports If x depends for its being on y, then x…
note: ST I q.104 a.1 co. (English translation) describes per se preservation as the case where 'what is preserved depends on the preserver in such a way that it cannot exist without it'. It ties one kind of dependence (of being on a cause of being) to the impossibility of being without. The premise asserts it for every dependence for being in the counterfactual sense of DEF-DEPENDS-FOR-BEING; the article contrasts this with dependence of becoming only (the builder), which does not exclude the effect's being without the cause.
